approach: Add an optional `mirrored_sources` section to the job plan. One entry has `content` (what the job writes), `source` (the governing source), `places` (every place in the source the content depends on) and `comparison` (the number of the criterion that compares the written content to those places). A new admission rule, `mirrored_sources_findings` in `plan_findings`, raises a major finding for an entry with a blank content or source, an empty or blank places list, or a comparison that is 0, out of range or has no demonstration. A major finding sends the plan back to the planner with no critic call, the same path as the `dependents` rule. The planner prompt requires the section and the critic prompt requires the critic to check it. The critic prompt also covers what a shape check cannot: a plan that writes mirrored content but gives `[]`, a places list that omits a place the critic's own search finds, and a comparing criterion that checks only structure. Those parts are prompt-only and marked so. The fixture is a plan whose entry names a source but lists no places. It is refused in the `plan_side` corpus, in unit tests in admission.rs, and end to end through the scripted planner in job_plan.rs. The same plan with the places listed is accepted. The section is stored on `JobPlan` with `serde(default)` and skipped when empty, so old records and plans with no mirrored content serialise as before. Prompt wording stays inside the budgets, and the `docs/system-facts.md` budget lines are updated to the computed values.

decisions.choice: Make the check a structured plan section with an admission shape rule, plus a critic prompt rule for what a shape check cannot see.
decisions.reason: The critic is a model, so a rejection of a plan with no list is not deterministic. A tested admission finding is. The defaults say a rule that matters is enforced by mechanism or marked prose-only, and the existing `dependents` section is the model: admission checks shape, the critic checks completeness against its own search.

rejected.why: A fixture cannot make a model critic reject; the rejection could not be tested and the user asked for a rejected fixture.

rejected.option: Fold the list into `dependents` through a new DependentKind variant
rejected.why: Smaller, but one entry per place cannot show a source with no places, and the entry has no field for the comparing criterion. The fixture would have nothing to reject.

rejected.option: Detect mirroring by keywords in the plan text or the reading's criteria (mirror, cache key, seed, definition)
rejected.why: The keywords hit unrelated plans, including this one, and the refusal rate would rise on a guess. Whether a plan mirrors a source is the planner's declaration, backed by the critic.

decisions.choice: The section is `Vec<PlanMirror>` with an empty list meaning the plan mirrors nothing; a missing key reads as empty.
decisions.reason: A plan that mirrors nothing needs no entry. It also leaves the existing plan JSON fixtures (fake.rs:379, lifecycle.rs:2669, introspection.rs:737, run/tests.rs:794, job_plan.rs:431) valid with no edits. `JobPlan.mirrored_sources` is skipped when empty, so old records re-serialise byte for byte.

rejected.option: Make the section required and refuse an empty list like `dependents`
rejected.why: Most plans mirror nothing and would be refused or padded. It would also force edits to six JSON fixtures in crates that are not deliverables.

rejected.option: Use `Option<Vec<_>>` so a missing key can be refused
rejected.why: It separates 'forgot' from '[]' but then needs every JSON fixture to carry the key. The critic prompt covers 'forgot' instead.

decisions.choice: The comparing criterion is checked only for shape: number in range, with one demonstration. Whether it compares content rather than structure stays with the critic.
decisions.reason: A deterministic check of the demonstration text would be a keyword guess. Athena cannot read the repository, and the existing rules also leave semantic checks to the critic.

rejected.option: Require the demonstration's `observes` to contain every place string
rejected.why: A place is often a long description, so the check would refuse good plans and pass a stuffed one.

decisions.choice: Show the section in `plan_body` in briefs.rs, only when non-empty, so the critic, a revision brief and the producer section all see the list.
decisions.reason: The critic cannot judge a list it is not shown, and the producer needs the places to write the content from. When it is empty the rendered bytes are unchanged, so existing producer-section hashes still match.

rejected.option: Leave it out of the briefs
rejected.why: The critic would see only the approach text.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of the planner prompt.
demonstrations.observes: A bullet states that a job writing content that summarises or mirrors a governing source must name the source, list every place in it the content depends on (each term mention, each compiled-in file for a cache key), and have one criterion that compares the written content to that list, not only its structure.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of the critic prompt.
demonstrations.observes: A bullet tells the critic to raise a major finding when such a plan has an empty `mirrored_sources`, a missing source, a places list that omits a place the critic finds by its own search, or a comparison criterion that checks only structure.

demonstrations.method: Run the tests whose names contain `mirrored_source`: admission unit tests, `plan_side` corpus cases and an end-to-end scripted-planner test. Each pairs a plan that names a source but lists no places (also blank source, blank place, comparison 0, comparison out of range) with the same plan with places listed.
demonstrations.observes: Each incomplete plan produces exactly one major Athena finding at location `mirrored sources, entry N` whose summary says the places list is missing. The scripted job sends the plan back to the planner with no critic call, then accepts the plan with the list. The complete fixture produces no finding.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `mirrored_sources_findings` the incomplete fixture yields no finding. The unit test in admission.rs, the `mirrored-source-no-places` corpus case and the job_plan.rs test (which expects the planner brief of round 2 to contain the finding text and zero critic calls) all fail. The complete-fixture cases pass either way, so they show the rule does not refuse good plans.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: `admission::plan_findings` (admission.rs:172) for the unit and corpus tests, and `Athena::go` with `Scenario.plans` for the end to end test. Fixtures: the corpus `plan_for` (refusal_corpus.rs:998) and admission.rs `plan_findings_for`, both passing a `JobPlan` as an argument, and the scripted fake planner in job_plan.rs (`scenario.plans`, line 856).
